These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Signal domain failures by raising ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a stable snake_case code as the first argument (e.g. "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity", "negative_amount") and a repr/detail string as the second, matching existing invoice.py functions.

texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Normalize unit prices with to_money and ZERO In ledgerly/invoice.py, convert line unit prices with to_money() and accumulate sums starting from the ZERO constant from ledgerly.money, as line_total and invoice_total already do.
texts.at-0003: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes Signal domain failures by raising ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a stable snake_case code as the first argument (e.g. "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity", "negative_amount") and a repr/detail string as the second, matching existing invoice.py functi
texts.at-0004: Guard draft-only mutations with invalid_state Mutating operations on an invoice must first check invoice.status != "draft" and raise BillingError("invalid_state", f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}"), as issue_invoice already does.
texts.at-0005: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc` before arithmetic; it rejects naive datetimes with `BillingError("naive_datetime", ...)`. Follow the pattern in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py:current_period`.
texts.at-0006: Money operations need idempotency_key Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. refund in ledgerly/adjustments.py) must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`; check ledgerly.audit.events() for an existing entry with that key first and return the orig
texts.at-0007: Refunds above 500 need second approver Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is missing.
texts.at-0008: Use money.to_money and round_money for amounts Convert incoming amounts with ledgerly.money.to_money (which rejects floats) and round results with ledgerly.money.round_money instead of built-in round(); do arithmetic in Decimal.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
[team convention] Money in ledgerly is Decimal end-to-end and always has exactly two decimal places. Never convert amounts to float.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Money-moving operations need idempotency_key
